    appearance [light | dark]

    increase_contrast [enabled | disabled]

	When invoked without arguments prints the current preferred content size category, from the following possible values:

    content_size [increment | decrement | desired_size]
	Set the preferred content size category. If 'increment' or 'decrement' is passed, the preferred content size will beset to the category one increment larger or smaller than the currently set value respectively.

state.title: Show simctl ui help

state.output:
Set up a device IO operation.
Usage: simctl io <device> <operation> <arguments>

Common arguments:
	    --display    Specifies which display to record. Accepts:
	                 - Screen ID (eg: "1") 
	                 - Screen name (eg: "Internal-1")
	                 - Screen device name (eg: "primary")
	                 - Screen UUID (eg: "D5293DAA-4D8C-453E-B049-969FE81936A0")
	                 - Port UUID (eg: "D5293DAA-4D8C-453E-B049-969FE81936A0"
	                 - Alias (for compatibility): "internal" or "external"
	                 Use 'simctl io <device> enumerate' to list available screens and their IDs.

Supported operations:
	enumerate [--poll]
	    Lists all available IO ports and descriptor states.
	    --poll       Poll after enumeration.

	poll
	    Polls all available IO ports for events.

	recordVideo [--codec=<codec>] [--display=<display>] [--mask=<policy>] [--force] <file or url>
	    Records the display to a QuickTime movie at the specified file or url.
	    --codec      Specifies the codec type: "h264" or "hevc". Default is "hevc".

	    --mask       For non-rectangular displays, handle the mask by policy:
	                 ignored: The mask is ignored and the unmasked framebuffer is saved.
	                 alpha: Not supported, but retained for compatibility; the mask is rendered black.
	                 black: The mask is rendered black.

	    --force      Force the output file to be written to, even if the file already exists.

	simctl writes 'Recording started' to stderr once the first video frame has been processed. Look for this
	if you want to wait for the recording to start.
	Send SIGINT (Control + C) to stop recording. simctl exits once the in-flight frames are processed
	and the video file is finalized.

	screenshot [--type=<type>] [--display=<display>] [--mask=<policy>] <file or url>
	    Saves a screenshot as a PNG to the specified file or url(use "-" for stdout).
	    --type       Can be "png", "tiff", "bmp", "gif", "jpeg". Default is png.

	    --mask       For non-rectangular displays, handle the mask by policy:
	                 ignored: The mask is ignored and the unmasked framebuffer is saved.
	                 alpha: The mask is used as premultiplied alpha.
	                 black: The mask is rendered black.

	screenConfig [--display=<display>] <subcommand> [arguments]
	    Manage device screen configuration.

	    power <on|off>
	        Set the power state of a screen.

	    geometry <width>x<height>[@<scale>]
	        Change the geometry of a screen.
	        The width and height must be compatible with the screen's current mode.
	        If @<scale> is specified, a mode with that scale factor will be selected.

Example:
	Save a screenshot of the booted device to screenshot.png:
	simctl io booted screenshot screenshot.png

OVERVIEW: Core Device Control: a command-line utility for exercising Core
Device functionality.

devicectl is a Core Device command-line utility that you can use to interact
with devices connected to this host. Automation and integration with other
tools is supported via JSON output captured to a file, which is versioned and
will remain stable across releases. Standard output is meant for human
consumption and is not guaranteed to be stable across releases.

USAGE: devicectl [--verbose] [--quiet] [--timeout <seconds>] [--json-output <path>] [--log-output <path>] <subcommand>

OUTPUT OPTIONS:
  -v, --verbose           If given, provide more logging output than normal.
  -q, --quiet             If given, output will include only errors.
  -t, --timeout <seconds> The overall command timeout in seconds. If this limit
                          is exceeded the command is abandoned as a failure.
  -j, --json-output <path>
                          An optional path to write a JSON file with command
                          results. Pass '-' (or '/dev/stdout' / '/dev/fd/1') to
                          write the JSON to stdout instead of a file.
        For a file path, both absolute and working-directory-relative forms are
        accepted; existing files are overwritten. Any of '-', '/dev/stdout',
        and '/dev/fd/1' selects stdout. When the JSON document is on stdout,
        human-readable output (progress, status, log lines) is routed to stderr
        instead. A few commands write non-JSON content to stdout themselves
        (binary payloads, bridged remote stdout, legal notices) and will reject
        stdout-selecting values at validation time — see each command's help
        for details.
  -l, --log-output <path> An optional path to write all logging otherwise
                          passed to stdout/stderr.

OPTIONS:
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  device                  Commands to interact with devices.
  diagnose                Gather diagnostic information for debugging or filing
                          bug reports.
  list                    List things that devicectl knows about.
  manage                  Commands to change state between the system and
                          devices, or between devices themselves.

  See 'devicectl help <subcommand>' for detailed help.

	                 - Screen device name (eg: "primary")
	                 - Screen UUID (eg: "D5293DAA-4D8C-453E-B049-969FE81936A0")

	                 - Alias (for compatibility): "internal" or "external"

Supported operations:
	enumerate [--poll]
	    Lists all available IO ports and descriptor states.
	    --poll       Poll after enumeration.

	poll
	    Polls all available IO ports for events.

	recordVideo [--codec=<codec>] [--display=<display>] [--mask=<policy>] [--force] <file or url>
	    Records the display to a QuickTime movie at the specified file or url.
	    --codec      Specifies the codec type: "h264" or "hevc". Default is "hevc".

	    --mask       For non-rectangular displays, handle the mask by policy:
	                 ignored: The mask is ignored and the unmasked framebuffer is saved.
	                 alpha: Not supported, but retained for compatibility; the mask is rendered black.
	                 black: The mask is rendered black.

	    --force      Force the output file to be written to, even if the file already exists.

	and the video file is finalized.

	    Saves a screenshot as a PNG to the specified file or url(use "-" for stdout).
	    --type       Can be "png", "tiff", "bmp", "gif", "jpeg". Default is png.

	    --mask       For non-rectangular displays, handle the mask by policy:
	                 ignored: The mask is ignored and the unmasked framebuffer is saved.
	                 alpha: The mask is used as premultiplied alpha.

	        The width and height must be compatible with the screen's current mode.
	        If @<scale> is specified, a mode with that scale factor will be selected.

part.text: I’m switching to a tiny XcodeGen-based UI test harness so I can drive the simulator with XCTest instead of unavailable touch tools. First step is creating the project scaffold.

input.patchText:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: ui-harness/project.yml
+name: Harness
+options:
+  bundleIdPrefix: com.example
+settings:
+  base:
+    IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: 15.0
+targets:
+  Harness:
+    type: application
+    platform: iOS
+    sources:
+      - path: Harness
+    settings:
+      GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES
+      PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.Harness
+      SWIFT_VERSION: 5.0
+  HarnessUITests:
+    type: bundle.ui-testing
+    platform: iOS
+    sources:
+      - path: HarnessUITests
+    dependencies:
+      - target: Harness
+    settings:
+      GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES
+      PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.HarnessUITests
+      SWIFT_VERSION: 5.0
*** Add File: ui-harness/Harness/HarnessApp.swift
+import SwiftUI
+
+@main
+struct HarnessApp: App {
+    var body: some Scene {
+        WindowGroup {
+            ContentView()
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+struct ContentView: View {
+    var body: some View {
+        Text("Harness")
+            .padding()
+    }
+}
*** Add File: ui-harness/HarnessUITests/SettingsNavigationUITests.swift
+import XCTest
+
+final class SettingsNavigationUITests: XCTestCase {
+    @MainActor
+    func testOpenSettingsHelpAbout() throws {
+        let springboard = XCUIApplication(bundleIdentifier: "com.apple.springboard")
+        let vector = XCUIApplication(bundleIdentifier: "im.vector.app")
+
+        if springboard.alerts.firstMatch.waitForExistence(timeout: 10) {
+            springboard.alerts.firstMatch.buttons["Open"].tap()
+        }
+
+        vector.activate()
+
+        let screen = vector.coordinate(withNormalizedOffset: CGVector(dx: 0.08, dy: 0.09))
+        screen.tap()
+        screen.tap()
+
+        sleep(2)
+        print(vector.debugDescription)
+    }
+}
*** End Patch
